pr.title: Play field keys through a track's effects, routed into the daemon through FieldOut (live-supercollider.md chunk 3)
pr.head: 5a51b4fda39e1d950c2d6b72d7a5a89b734e8f9f

summary: field keys plays a SuperCollider instrument from the computer keyboard. Its sound comes from a voice host, sclang driving its own scsynth. A song's effects, the inserts on each track and on the tracks above it up to main, run in another process, the daemon field-audiod. So until now, playing a track's instrument with field keys sounded dry, and the instrument's line said so.

This pull request is chunk 3 of the live-supercollider plan, the chunk you hear. Chunk 1 (#196) taught a live session to read an input from outside the session and carry it up through every chain above its track. Chunk 2 (#198) added FieldOut, a SuperCollider plugin that writes audio into a shared-memory ring the daemon reads. This chunk connects the two. field keys <track> opens an input for each armed track, loads the song with those inputs, and has the voice host write each track's voice into its ring. With the transport stopped, the daemon now plays the inputs over silence.

The review of this head requested changes in five threads, and each one is flagged on the line it is about. Inputs stay open when field keys fails after routing, and the daemon then never exits. Another field play drops the input windows. Nothing ties the voice host to the daemon's device and rate. On Linux the plugin path loses SuperCollider's core UGens. And the voice contract still says out is bus 0.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Voice host: sc/voice-host.scd running in sclang. It boots its own scsynth and turns MIDI into voices.
  • Input: a named source the daemon reads each block. field keys names its inputs keys:<song>/<track>.
  • Ring: the shared-memory buffer behind an input. FieldOut writes it and the daemon reads it.
  • FieldOut: the scsynth plugin that writes into a ring.
  • Route: the synth field-route, which carries one instrument's private bus into FieldOut.
  • Overlay: a second instance of each chain on an input's path, which the daemon runs beside the song.
  • Idle path: the overlay through a second instance of main's chain, played while the transport is stopped.
  • Converted delivery: the daemon resampling the song because the device cannot run at the song's rate.
  • Dry note: the end of the instrument's line, · dry: the effects on … are not heard.

cards.title: Review of 5a51b4f: changes requested
cards.html:
• Orphaned inputs. A field keys that fails after routing, or is killed, leaves its input open, and inputsOpen() then keeps the daemon from ever exiting idle.
  • Session loads drop the input. field play, its watch, and field ui load sessions without the input window, which silences the routed voice.
  • Device and rate. The voice host boots on --device or the system output, not on the daemon's device. Under converted delivery the routed voice is silent while the transport is stopped.
  • Linux plugins. ugenPluginsPath replaces scsynth's defaults and leaves out the core UGens.
  • Voice contract. The docs still say the host sets out to bus 0.

The first three were reproduced at this head against null-output daemons. The Linux one rests on SuperCollider's source.

cards.title: Left for later
cards.html:
• Criterion 3, hearing a track through its effects, is the author's to check by ear.
  • Criteria 4 and 5, the added latency and an hour without a dropout, need a real device.
  • A session swap under a playing input rebuilds the overlay cold, a gap of the path's latency. §10 accepts that for now.
  • The end-to-end test routing-voice.test.ts needs SuperCollider and an output device, so it skips on CI.

groups.title: What crosses between the processes
groups.kicker: The route SynthDef that Field writes, and the input's new peak in status
intro: Three processes take part when you play a track: field keys in Node, the voice host, and the daemon. This group holds the two small contracts between them that change.

The route is a SynthDef, SuperCollider's compiled synth definition. It reads two channels from a bus and hands them to FieldOut. sclang has no FieldOut class to build that SynthDef from, so routeSynthDef writes its binary form directly.
Each open input in the daemon's status now reports peak, the loudest sample read since a client last asked. Every client status read resets it.

files.note: Adds routeSynthDef: In.ar(in, 2) into FieldOut.ar(ring, …), with in and ring as controls.

checks.text: Ran src/audiod/live-ring.test.ts at this head. A non-realtime scsynth loads this SynthDef, and a sine on private bus 20 reaches the daemon's ring through it.
peak is required, so this CLI rejects the status of a daemon that has live-input but no peak. Only builds of this stack's chunks 1 and 2 are such a daemon.

groups.title: The daemon plays inputs while the song is stopped
groups.kicker: A second instance of the output chain, a pin against the idle exit, a peak meter, and a file-to-ring feeder
intro: Chunk 1 gave a live session input windows: a track reads audio from outside the session each block. What an input reaches travels in the overlay, a second instance of each chain on the input's path, summed into main, the output track, before main's own chain runs. Until now that happened only while the transport played.

With the transport stopped, Player::pullAudio now calls LiveSession::renderIdle when the session has inputs. It renders the overlay at the stopped position and runs it through idleChain, a second instance of the output track's chain. You hear what you play over silence, and the song's own chain and position stay where they were.
Converted delivery is how the daemon plays a song whose rate the device cannot run at: it resamples. It has no idle path, so a stopped session is silent then.

Three smaller pieces ride along. An open input keeps the daemon from exiting idle (Player::inputsOpen). Each input meters its peak. And field-audiod --ring-feed <ring> <file.wav> writes a file into a ring at real-time pace, as FieldOut would, so an input can be tested without SuperCollider.

checks.text: A limiter or hosted plugin emits fewer samples than it takes while it fills its lookahead. Each chain's output therefore passes through a FIFO that starts with the chain's latency in zeros, so every block leaves whole and exactly that late (live-supercollider.md §9, step 4). idleDelayed is that FIFO for the idle chain.

files.note: Declares renderIdle, hasInputs, and the idle chain's buffers.
Builds the idle chain at load, and adds renderIdle.

checks.text: Traced renderOverlay: it skips the chain for the output track, so overlay[slot].post is the sum before main's chain, and renderIdle applies that chain once. The FIFO starts with exactly the chain's latency, so a voice is as late with the transport stopped as playing.

Nothing here allocates on the audio thread. idleBlock and idleDelayed are reserved at load, 16384 frames plus the latency, and a block stays inside them. buildOverlay runs in the LiveSession constructor, so the idle chain's second instance of a hosted plugin is made off the audio thread.

The comment says field keys may play through an input with nothing else connected. But while field keys plays, the connection that routeArmed holds already keeps the daemon up. So the pin acts only after field keys has gone, which the flag on src/commands/keys.ts line 93 is about.

files.note: Plays a stopped live session's inputs through renderIdle, and passes consumePeak to each ring's stats.

checks.text: The idle branch runs under the same ScopedTryLock on liveLock as the playing path, so it never reads a session in the middle of a swap.

files.note: Tracks the loudest sample read, and adds runRingFeed for --ring-feed.

checks.text: peak has one writer, the audio thread, and a status read exchanges it back to 0. Relaxed atomics are enough for a meter.

files.note: Adds --ring-feed, and keeps the daemon from exiting idle while an input is open.

checks.text: A ring that does not parse as a number reads as 0, and the daemon then starts as a server instead of failing. The review lists this as a suggestion.

groups.title: The voice host writes into rings
groups.kicker: Each routed instrument's voices play into a private bus that its route carries into the ring
intro: The voice host is sc/voice-host.scd running in sclang. It boots its own scsynth and plays each armed instrument's voice from every MIDI source. Several instruments play in unison: each note sounds a voice from each.

VoiceHost.start now takes rings, one per instrument, each a ring number or null to play straight to the device. It also takes fieldOut, the directory that holds the built plugin. When any ring is set, it writes the route SynthDef to a temp file and passes FIELD_RINGS, FIELD_FIELDOUT, and FIELD_ROUTE_DEF to the host.

At each boot the host loads the route and gives each routed instrument a two-channel private bus. It then starts one route per bus at the tail of the default group, after every voice. A routed voice's out control is that bus, not bus 0.

scsynth crashes when it quits with a FieldOut still running, because it unloads plugins before it frees synths. So every way the host stops frees all nodes first. VoiceHost.close sends /g_freeAll before /quit, and both the rate restart and the parent-gone check call stopRoutes.

files.note: Starts and stops the routes, adds FieldOut to the plugin path, and sends each voice to its bus.

checks.text: On Linux the routed scsynth loads no core UGens, so the voice is silent. Setting ugenPluginsPath passes -U, and scsynth then searches only the listed paths. Platform.resourceDir +/+ "plugins" is <prefix>/share/SuperCollider/plugins on Linux, but the core UGens live in <prefix>/lib/SuperCollider/plugins. Adding FieldOut through SC_PLUGIN_PATH keeps the defaults.

Routing makes out a private bus, but docs/keys.md and keyboard-instrument.md §2.6 still tell instrument authors that the host sets out to bus 0. A voice that writes to bus 0 in voice mode bypasses the route and plays dry, while the line says the effects are heard.
A rate restart calls stopRoutes before server.quit. boot loads the route with d_load and runs startRoutes every time, so the routes come back on the new server with fresh buses.

files.note: Takes rings and fieldOut, writes the route SynthDef, finds the built FieldOut with fieldOutPluginDir, and frees all nodes before /quit.

checks.text: Ran src/keys/voice-host.test.ts at this head. The host receives FIELD_RINGS, FIELD_FIELDOUT, and a route file that starts with SCgf, and /g_freeAll reaches the server before /quit.
Each start leaves a field-route-* directory in the temp directory, and nothing removes it. The review lists this as a suggestion.

groups.title: field keys routes armed tracks through the daemon
groups.kicker: Open an input per track, load the song with them, and give the voice host the rings
intro: field keys creek/track:bass arms the MIDI track bass and plays the instrument that the track names. Before this change, the voice always played straight to the device. The effects on bass and on the tracks above it were not heard, and the instrument's line ended with a dry note: · dry: the effects on keys-bus are not heard yet.
Now play calls routeArmed before the voice host starts, and it does three things:

1. Opens an input for each armed track. It asks the daemon for an input named keys:<song>/<track>, which answers with a ring number.
  2. Loads the song's live session with those inputs. It compiles the song with an input window on each armed track and loads it, which replaces whatever the daemon had loaded.
  3. Hands the rings to the voice host. Each armed entry becomes its own instrument with its own ring, so two tracks that share an instrument still get separate voices. An instrument named without a track gets null and plays straight to the device.

When routing is not possible, routeArmed returns a reason, and the dry note shows it. The reasons are tracks in two songs, Windows, FieldOut not built, a daemon without live-input, or the first line of any error. On quit, play closes the voice host first, then the inputs, and then loads the song again without them.

files.note: New. routeArmed opens the inputs, loads the session, and returns the rings, or the reason it cannot.

checks.text: The input window exists only in the session that this function compiles. field play creek in another terminal, a structural edit under field play --watch, or field ui loads a session without it, and the daemon stops reading the ring. Reproduced at this head: after such a load, half a second of --ring-feed read 0 frames, stopped and playing.
AudiodClient.connect sits outside the try. A daemon that never answers then ends field keys with an error instead of the dry fallback. The review lists this as a suggestion.

files.note: Calls routeArmed, gives the voice host the rings, drops the dry note when routed, and closes the routing on quit.

checks.text: Only the quit path closes the routing. If KeysHelper.start or VoiceHost.start throws, or field keys is killed, keys:<song>/<track> stays open. Player::inputsOpen() then keeps the daemon up for good, and the next routed field keys on that track plays dry because the input is already open. Reproduced at this head.

The voice host still boots on --device or the system output, while the routed voice is heard on the daemon's device. When the two differ, the line names a device you are not hearing, and the ring crosses two clocks. When the device cannot run at the song's rate, the routed voice is silent while the transport is stopped. Reproduced at this head with a 44100 Hz song.
Ran src/commands/keys.test.ts: the line drops the dry note when routed, and gives the reason when routing was not possible.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: From the instrument line up to a note through real sclang and scsynth
intro:
• routing.test.ts runs routeArmed against a null-output daemon, with an empty FieldOut.scx standing in for the build. It opens keys:creek/bass, loads creek with it, puts the song back on close, and checks each reason it cannot route.
  • routing-voice.test.ts runs the whole path through real sclang and scsynth with FieldOut: a note from a published MIDI source reaches the track's input. It needs SuperCollider and an output device, so it runs on a workstation and skips on CI.
  • live-ring.test.ts feeds a ring with --ring-feed while the transport is stopped, reads the sine's 0.25 peak back through the idle path, and checks the route in a non-realtime scsynth.
  • voice-host.test.ts and keys.test.ts check what the host receives, the free before /quit, and the dry note.

checks.text: Ran routing.test.ts, live-ring.test.ts, voice-host.test.ts, and keys.test.ts at this head with FIELD_AUDIOD set: 32 passed. Every ring they opened was gone from shared memory afterward.
routing-voice.test.ts was read but not run in the review, because it opens the output device and connects every MIDI source.
